subject: Consolidating seats + feature marketplace — packaging options
messages:

Cc: procurement@brightleafhealth.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring seat consolidation + feature marketplace for pilot

Hi Neha —

Thanks again for the demo last week. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we scope the pilot:

- We currently have 120 named seats across three teams but heavy idle time during off-peak. Would Redwood support a seat-pool / compression approach (e.g., 60 pooled seats with burst capacity) while preserving per-seat feature entitlements?
- We liked the idea of an add-on marketplace for higher-accuracy rerank and domain adapters — can those be attached per-seat or per-organization?
- Can you share packaging/pricing scenarios (compact vs full) including any seat-credit conversion math and likely discounts at ~12-month committed pilots?

I attached our RFP features spreadsheet. Procurement is looped for commercial constraints.

Appreciate a quick sketch so we can decide whether to proceed with a 6–12 week pilot.

Thanks,
Maria
Director, Product Ops
BrightLeaf Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Exploring seat consolidation + feature marketplace for pilot

Hi Maria —

Great questions — high level answers below and Ben + Marcus are on thread to add pricing and product constraints:

1) Seat pooling / compression
- We support pooled seat licensing for concurrent usage (you buy N concurrency tokens instead of N named seats). For your profile (120 seats, < 60% peak concurrency) the math often favors a 50–60% reduction in token count for steady-state.
- Burst capacity: you can add a dedicated burst bucket that charges only when used. Typical pilot structure: base pooled tokens + small reserved burst to avoid throttling.

2) Feature marketplace & entitlements
- Marketplace add-ons (rerank, domain adapters, retrieval connectors) can be assigned at org level or to seat groups. Per-seat gating is possible but increases provisioning complexity and admin overhead. 
- For pilots we recommend org-level entitlements with role-based overrides for a few power users.

3) Packaging/pricing scenarios (sketch)
- Compact Pilot: pooled tokens = 70, org add-ons enabled, no dedicated burst. Monthly effective cost = metered token usage + add-on metering; lower committed discount.
- Full Pilot: pooled tokens = 90, small dedicated burst bucket, org add-ons + 10 licensed power seats for premium features. Higher commit discount + onboarding credits.

Ben — can you drop ballpark numbers and recommend a discount cadence for a 12-month pilot with a mid-sized pilot commitment? Marcus — quick note on any technical limits to per-seat adapters?

Thanks,
Neha
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Torres <maria@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring seat consolidation + feature marketplace for pilot

Hi Maria —

Thanks Neha. Maria — here are two commercial sketches to move the conversation forward (all numbers illustrative, we can refine):

Option A — Compact Pilot (12 months)
- Base: 70 pooled concurrency tokens (equiv. to ~120 named seats with compression)
- Add-ons: org-level rerank + domain adaptor enabled (metered)
- Burst bucket: none
- Commitment: $85k annual commit (payable monthly)
- Discount: 8% off list for 12-month pilot
- Onboarding: $7k credit applied to first invoice

Option B — Full Pilot (12 months)
- Base: 90 pooled tokens + 10 premium seats (licensed power users)
- Add-ons: rerank + domain adaptor included up to capped usage, overage metered
- Burst bucket: small reserved (100k tokens/mo)
- Commitment: $135k annual commit
- Discount: 15% off list for 12-month pilot
- Onboarding: $12k credit + two technical office hours per week during ramp

Seat-credit conversion note: we amortize named seat equivalence by observed concurrency. If you provide a 30-day token trace we’ll run a compression estimate and propose exact token counts.

If procurement needs net‑net pricing or PO terms, we can surface those in an SOW addendum. Would you like me to prepare a redlined pilot quote for procurement?

—Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales

From: Maria Torres <maria@brightleafhealth.com>

Neha / Ben —

Appreciate the clear sketches — that helps a lot. A few asks before we proceed:

- Could you move Option A to a 10% pilot discount if we commit to a 12-month PO within two weeks? Procurement is asking for a small concession vs your starter off.
- Please confirm SLA/uptime guarantees for the pilot environment and whether the burst bucket will be prioritized over other customers in the same region.
- Marcus — can you confirm that the domain adaptor will accept our proprietary embeddings format (we included example formats in the RFP spreadsheet). If not, what engineering lift is required?

If we can get the 10% and SLAs confirmed, procurement will prepare a PO and we’ll kick off a pilot onboarding call next week.

Thanks,
Maria

BrightLeaf Health
